entries.snippet: Windows 11 Screen Reader Manual: step-by-step keyboard and screen-reader instructions, practice, troubleshooting, and command references.
entries.text: windows 11 screen reader manual - accessible learning center skip to main content accessible learning center manual windows 11 screen reader manual narrator, nvda, and jaws independent self-study guide all manuals table of contents start of manual purpose: this manual is written directly to a person learning windows 11 with a screen reader. it assumes little or no prior experience and explains exactly what to press, what you should hear, and how to recover when the result is different. three screen readers: narrator is built into windows 11. nvda is a free third-party screen reader from nv access. jaws is a commercial screen reader from freedom scientific. their commands are not interchangeable. command labels: every procedure identifies whether a command belongs to windows, narrator, nvda, or jaws. how to use this manual begin with parts 1-12 even if you eventually plan to use nvda or jaws. these sections teach windows 11 keyboard navigation that all three screen readers rely on. do one action, stop, and listen to what changed before pressing another key. tab normally moves forward through controls. shift+tab moves backward. arrow keys normally move within lists, menus, radio-button groups, tree views, and text. enter activates many buttons, links, selected files, and menu commands. spacebar toggles checkboxes and many buttons. escape closes menus/dialogs or backs out of temporary interfaces. alt+tab switches among open applications. windows key opens start. windows+s opens search. learn windows keyboard navigation first, then add the commands for your chosen screen reader. table of contents part 1 - what a screen reader does part 2 - windows 11 keyboard foundations part 3 - start, search, taskbar, and switching apps part 4 - windows settings part 5 - file explorer part 6 - dialog boxes, menus, and common controls part 7 - reading and editing text part 8 - web browsing concepts part 9 - notifications, quick settings, and system tray part 10 - copy, cut, paste, rename, and delete part 11 - keyboard troubleshooting and recovery part 12 - choosing narrator, nvda, or jaws part 13 - narrator: start, stop, and narrator key part 14 - narrator: input learning and basic navigation part 15 - narrator: scan mode part 16 - narrator: reading text and views part 17 - narrator: web navigation part 18 - narrator: settings, speech, verbosity, and punctuation part 19 - narrator: braille part 20 - narrator: troubleshooting part 21 - nvda: start, stop, and nvda key part 22 - nvda: basic navigation and speech part 23 - nvda: browse mode and web navigation part 24 - nvda: settings, add-ons, and braille part 25 - nvda: troubleshooting part 26 - jaws: start, stop, and jaws key part 27 - jaws: basic reading and help part 28 - jaws: virtual cursor and web navigation part 29 - jaws: forms, lists, and windows explorer part 30 - jaws: settings, quick settings, and braille part 31 - jaws: troubleshooting part 32 - comparing narrator, nvda, and jaws part 33 - independent practice course part 34 - quick reference commands part 35 - official resources part 1 - what a screen reader does a screen reader converts information from the windows interface into speech and, when connected, refreshable braille. it follows keyboard focus, a screen-reader cursor, browse/scan mode, or another navigation system. focus is the windows control currently ready to receive input. a button performs an action. a checkbox can be checked or unchecked. a combo box lets you choose from a list. an edit field is where you type text. a dialog box asks for information or a decision. a screen reader usually announces both the control name and control type. part 2 - windows 11 keyboard foundations task command next control tab previous control shift+tab activate enter toggle checkbox/button spacebar move in list/menu arrow keys close/back escape context menu shift+f10 switch applications alt+tab close window alt+f4 2.1 navigate a window with tab what you will learn: move through controls without a mouse. before you begin: open settings or another simple windows app. exactly how to do it press tab once. listen to the focused control. press tab again. continue through five controls. press shift+tab twice to move backward. if focus enters a list, use up/down arrow. press escape if a menu opens accidentally. what should happen: focus moves from control to control. if that does not happen: if tab seems stuck, press escape once, then tab again. if focus is in a list, use arrow keys. practice: move forward ten controls and backward five. part 3 - start, search, taskbar, and switching apps 3.1 open an app from start/search what you will learn: launch programs without locating desktop icons. before you begin: be anywhere in windows. exactly how to do it press the windows key. type the app name, for example notepad. wait for search results. use up/down arrow if multiple results appear. press enter on the correct result. what should happen: the app opens. if that does not happen: if the wrong result opens, press alt+f4 and search using a more specific name. practice: open notepad, settings, and calculator. 3.2 switch between open apps what you will learn: move among running applications. before you begin: open at least two apps. exactly how to do it hold alt. press tab repeatedly while holding alt. listen to each app name. release alt on the desired app. what should happen: the selected app receives focus. if that does not happen: if it is not listed, it may not be open. practice: switch between notepad and settings three times. 3.3 use the taskbar what you will learn: reach pinned/running apps. before you begin: be anywhere in windows. exactly how to do it press windows+t. use left/right arrow through taskbar items. press enter to open or switch to the selected app. press escape when finished. what should happen: taskbar focus moves among apps. if that does not happen: if windows+t seems silent, press it again and listen for a taskbar item. practice: open one pinned app. part 4 - windows settings 4.1 open and search settings what you will learn: find a windows option efficiently. before you begin: be anywhere in windows. exactly how to do it press windows+i. wait for settings. tab to the search box if needed. type narrator, bluetooth, sound, or accessibility. use down arrow through results. press enter on the desired result. use tab/shift+tab through controls. what should happen: the requested settings page opens. if that does not happen: if the exact phrase is not found, search with a broader word. practice: find accessibility > narrator. part 5 - file explorer 5.1 open file explorer what you will learn: browse folders and files. before you begin: be anywhere in windows. exactly how to do it press windows+e. wait for file explorer. press tab through major panes. when focus is in the file list, use arrow keys through files. press enter to open a folder/file. press alt+left arrow to go back. press alt+up arrow to move up one folder. what should happen: you can enter and leave folders. if that does not happen: if arrow keys do not move files, press tab until the file list is focused. practice: open documents, enter a folder, then return. 5.2 rename a file or folder what you will learn: change an item's name. before you begin: select a practice item. exactly how to do it move to the item. press f2. type the new name. press enter. listen to confirm the new name. what should happen: the item is renamed. if that does not happen: if f2 does nothing, confirm the file itself is selected. practice: rename a practice file and rename it back. part 6 - dialog boxes, menus, and common controls button: enter or spacebar. checkbox: spacebar toggles. radio buttons: arrow keys. combo box: alt+down arrow opens, arrows choose, enter confirms. tabs: ctrl+tab / ctrl+shift+tab often changes tabs. context menu: shift+f10. menus: alt or f10 can expose menus in many desktop apps. 6.1 use a combo box what you will learn: choose an option in a drop

entries.title: Zoom Manual
entries.snippet: Zoom Manual: step-by-step keyboard and screen-reader instructions, practice, troubleshooting, and command references.
entries.text: zoom manual - accessible learning center skip to main content accessible learning center manual zoom manual meetings, chat, screen sharing, accessibility, and screen readers independent self-study guide all manuals table of contents start of manual official zoom workplace getting started guide purpose: this manual is written directly to the person learning zoom. it assumes you may be opening zoom for the first time. every procedure explains where to go, exactly what to click or press, what should happen, and what to do if the result is different. current interface: zoom states that the zoom workplace desktop interface was updated in version 6.7.0. this manual uses that current interface as its reference while explaining alternatives when a toolbar item is under more or has been customized. important: meeting features can be disabled or restricted by the host, account administrator, organization, license, or meeting policy. if a control described here is missing, that does not always mean you are doing something wrong. how to use this manual work through parts 1-8 first if zoom is completely new to you. do one action at a time, then stop and confirm what changed. tab moves forward through many buttons and fields. shift+tab moves backward. enter or spacebar activates many focused controls. escape closes many menus, dialogs, and temporary panels. windows and mac shortcuts are shown separately when they differ. screen-reader users should listen to both the control name and the control type before activating it. zoom lets users customize toolbar placement, and hosts/admins can restrict features. use the control name rather than assuming it is always in the same position. use zoom settings > keyboard shortcuts to review the exact shortcuts available in your installed version. table of contents part 1 - what zoom is part 2 - install, open, and sign in part 3 - learn the zoom workplace window part 4 - essential keyboard navigation part 5 - join a meeting from a link part 6 - join with meeting id and passcode part 7 - test audio, microphone, speaker, and camera part 8 - understand the meeting window part 9 - mute and unmute part 10 - start and stop video part 11 - participants part 12 - in-meeting chat part 13 - captions and accessibility part 14 - raise hand, reactions, and non-verbal feedback part 15 - share your screen or a window part 16 - leave a meeting part 17 - schedule a meeting part 18 - start a meeting you host part 19 - invite others part 20 - host and security controls part 21 - waiting room part 22 - breakout rooms part 23 - recording part 24 - zoom team chat part 25 - profile, status, and settings part 26 - keyboard shortcuts part 27 - windows screen reader use part 28 - voiceover on mac part 29 - zoom web app part 30 - zoom mobile app part 31 - troubleshooting part 32 - independent practice course part 33 - quick reference part 34 - official zoom resources part 1 - what zoom is zoom workplace is a collaboration application that can include meetings, team chat, phone, calendar, mail, whiteboard, and other tools depending on your account. this manual focuses primarily on the features most people need to participate independently in zoom meetings. a zoom meeting is an online session where participants can use audio, video, chat, captions, reactions, screen sharing, and other features. a host starts or controls the meeting. a co-host can be given many host controls. a participant joins the meeting and can use the controls allowed by the host. a waiting room can hold participants before the host admits them. a meeting id identifies a meeting. some meetings also require a passcode. a join link can contain enough information to open the correct meeting directly. zoom workplace desktop app is different from the zoom web portal. the desktop app is used for meetings and local app settings; the web portal contains many account-level settings. part 2 - install, open, and sign in 2.1 open zoom workplace on windows what you will learn: open zoom using only the keyboard. before you begin: zoom workplace must already be installed. exactly how to do it press the windows key. type zoom workplace. wait for the zoom workplace app to appear in windows search. press enter. wait for the zoom window to open. if the first screen gives you sign in, join a meeting, or sign up, choose sign in if you have an account and want access to your scheduled meetings/settings. use tab to move to sign in and press enter if necessary. enter the account information requested by zoom or your organization. complete any browser-based, single-sign-on, password, or verification prompts. return to the zoom workplace app and wait until its main window finishes loading. what should happen: the main zoom workplace window opens with your account signed in. if that does not happen: if zoom does not appear in windows search, it may not be installed. if your organization uses sso, make sure you choose the correct sign-in method rather than repeatedly entering a personal zoom password. practice: close zoom, reopen it from windows search, and identify whether you are signed in. 2.2 open zoom workplace on a mac what you will learn: open zoom from spotlight. before you begin: zoom workplace must already be installed. exactly how to do it press command+space. type zoom workplace. press return. wait for the app to open. use tab or voiceover navigation to move to sign in if needed. choose the correct sign-in method. complete password, browser, sso, or verification steps. return to zoom after authentication. what should happen: zoom workplace opens and displays the signed-in app. if that does not happen: if spotlight cannot find zoom workplace, check the applications folder or install the current zoom workplace app. practice: quit and reopen zoom once. part 3 - learn the zoom workplace window zoom's main app window can include home, meetings/calendar, team chat, contacts, whiteboards, and additional products. zoom notes that the desktop interface changed in version 6.7.0, so the exact navigation bar may differ from older instructions. navigation bar: switches among zoom products and work areas. home: shows upcoming meetings and common actions such as join, new meeting, or schedule. meetings or calendar: displays scheduled meetings/events depending on your account integration. team chat: displays zoom chat conversations and channels. profile picture/account menu: opens status, account controls, settings, and update options. settings: contains audio, video, accessibility, keyboard shortcuts, and other preferences. meeting window: opens separately when you start or join a meeting. 3.1 explore the zoom window with tab what you will learn: learn where keyboard focus moves before activating controls. before you begin: zoom workplace is open. exactly how to do it press tab once. listen to or visually identify the focused item. press tab again. continue through several controls. press shift+tab to move backward. when focus enters a list, try up arrow and down arrow to move within the list. press escape if you enter a temporary menu or pane that you do not want to use. continue until you can identify the navigation area, central content, and profile/settings controls. what should happen: you can move through the app without clicking random controls. if that does not happen: if tab appears to stop moving, try escape once, then tab again. if focus is inside a list, use arrow keys. practice: explore the home screen for two minutes without starting or joining a meeting. part 4 - essential keyboard navigation task windows mac mute/unmute audio alt+a command+shift+a temporarily unmute while holding space hold space while muted and meeting window has focus hold space while muted and meeting window has focus start/stop video alt+v command+shift+v start/stop screen share alt+s command+shift+s open/close in-meeting chat alt+h command+shift+h open/close participants alt+u command+u raise/lower hand alt+y option+y switch s

using the keyboard. basic how-tos advanced how-tos command list basic how-tos join a meeting safely what you will learn: complete join a meeting safely independently with keyboard or screen-reader feedback. before you begin: open the relevant application or device screen and use a fictional, public, or nonprivate practice item. exactly how to do it keyboard commands: tab and shift+tab move through join controls. space changes a focused checkbox. enter activates join. open the invitation and verify the organizer, date, and meeting link. open the link and confirm the meeting application or browser tab. tab through microphone, camera, name, and audio choices. join muted unless instructed otherwise. activate join and wait for the meeting title or waiting-room announcement. what should happen: your microphone and camera states, followed by the meeting or waiting room. if that does not happen: do not press join repeatedly. check for a browser permission dialog or an “open application” prompt. practice: repeat join a meeting safely with a second safe practice item, then explain the commands you used. mute or unmute what you will learn: complete mute or unmute independently with keyboard or screen-reader feedback. before you begin: open the relevant application or device screen and use a fictional, public, or nonprivate practice item. exactly how to do it keyboard commands: zoom: alt+a. teams: ctrl+shift+m. google meet: ctrl+d. confirm the correct meeting is active. press the command once. wait for a spoken or sound confirmation. when uncertain, tab to the microphone button and read its state. what should happen: the intended item, setting, or result is available and can be verified before you continue. if that does not happen: do not toggle repeatedly. a host or organization may prevent unmuting. practice: repeat mute or unmute with a second safe practice item, then explain the commands you used. start or stop the camera what you will learn: complete start or stop the camera independently with keyboard or screen-reader feedback. before you begin: open the relevant application or device screen and use a fictional, public, or nonprivate practice item. exactly how to do it keyboard commands: zoom: alt+v. teams: ctrl+shift+o. google meet: ctrl+e. confirm the meeting and whether video is appropriate. press the correct command once. listen for “start video” or “stop video,” which usually describes the action available next. what should happen: the intended item, setting, or result is available and can be verified before you continue. if that does not happen: locate the camera button and check camera permissions or host restrictions. practice: repeat start or stop the camera with a second safe practice item, then explain the commands you used. open chat and send a message what you will learn: complete open chat and send a message independently with keyboard or screen-reader feedback. before you begin: open the relevant application or device screen and use a fictional, public, or nonprivate practice item. exactly how to do it keyboard command: zoom: alt+h opens or closes meeting chat. in teams and meet, locate chat by button navigation because shortcuts and layouts change. open chat and confirm its heading. move to the message field. type a short message and review it. press enter to send only when the application indicates enter sends. return to meeting controls after confirming the message appeared. what should happen: the intended item, setting, or result is available and can be verified before you continue. if that does not happen: check whether focus is in chat history, a recipient selector, or the message field. practice: repeat open chat and send a message with a second safe practice item, then explain the commands you used. advanced how-tos raise and lower your hand what you will learn: complete raise and lower your hand independently with keyboard or screen-reader feedback. before you begin: open the relevant application or device screen and use a fictional, public, or nonprivate practice item. exactly how to do it keyboard command: zoom: alt+y. in teams and meet, locate reactions or raise hand by its button name. activate raise hand once. listen for confirmation. wait to be recognized. lower your hand after speaking. what should happen: the intended item, setting, or result is available and can be verified before you continue. if that does not happen: find the button and read whether its current action is raise hand or lower hand. practice: repeat raise and lower your hand with a second safe practice item, then explain the commands you used. turn captions on what you will learn: complete turn captions on independently with keyboard or screen-reader feedback. before you begin: open the relevant application or device screen and use a fictional, public, or nonprivate practice item. exactly how to do it keyboard approach: navigate to captions, closed captions, or more actions, then activate the captions control. open captions before important discussion begins. select the spoken language if requested. confirm that caption text is appearing. remember that automatic captions may misidentify names or technical words. what should happen: the intended item, setting, or result is available and can be verified before you continue. if that does not happen: ask the host whether captions are enabled and request an accessible transcript or notes. practice: repeat turn captions on with a second safe practice item, then explain the commands you used. share a window safely what you will learn: complete share a window safely independently with keyboard or screen-reader feedback. before you begin: open the relevant application or device screen and use a fictional, public, or nonprivate practice item. exactly how to do it keyboard command: zoom: alt+s starts or stops sharing when permitted. for teams and meet, activate the labeled share control. close private files, messages, and notifications. open only the content you intend to share. start sharing and choose a specific window rather than the entire screen. read the selected window name before confirming. describe visual content aloud and provide the source file or accessible alternative. stop sharing and confirm that sharing ended. what should happen: the intended item, setting, or result is available and can be verified before you continue. if that does not happen: cancel the chooser. never select a source whose name you cannot verify. practice: repeat share a window safely with a second safe practice item, then explain the commands you used. leave without ending the meeting for everyone what you will learn: complete leave without ending the meeting for everyone independently with keyboard or screen-reader feedback. before you begin: open the relevant application or device screen and use a fictional, public, or nonprivate practice item. exactly how to do it keyboard approach: find leave, then read the confirmation choices. save anything needed from chat according to the meeting policy. activate leave. if you are the host, choose leave meeting unless you truly intend to end it for everyone. confirm that focus returns to the desktop or previous application. what should happen: the intended item, setting, or result is available and can be verified before you continue. if that does not happen: read the dialog carefully; do not choose end meeting for all by accident. practice: repeat leave without ending the meeting for everyone with a second safe practice item, then explain the commands you used. quick command list zoom alt+a / teams ctrl+shift+m / meet ctrl+d: microphone zoom alt+v / teams ctrl+shift+o / meet entries.text: windows 11 final quiz accessible five-question final quiz and printable completion certificate for windows 11. windows 11 final quiz - accessible learning center course completion quiz windows 11 final quiz answer five questions about the skills covered in this course. a score of 80 percent, or four correct answers, earns a printable course-completion certificate. windows 11 manual review lesson 10 all windows 11 lessons help and resource search final quiz choose one answer for every question. you may review the lessons and retake the quiz as many times as needed. 1. which windows shortcut opens file explorer? windows+e ctrl+e alt+e 2. what is the safest first step before moving or deleting a file? confirm its name and location rename every file empty the recycle bin 3. which shortcut switches among open applications? alt+tab ctrl+tab windows+r 4. where should related work files be kept?
